feedback: If the child says people live on the Moon now: Apollo astronauts walked there long ago, but nobody lives there today; today's astronauts live on the Station circling close to Earth.
If the child places the Station far out among the stars: show it orbiting close around Earth.
activities.intendedInsight: The landmark facts — astronaut = person who goes to space, people walked on the Moon in the past, the ISS is where they live and work now — can be recalled and distinguished.
learnerActions: Answer 'What is an astronaut?' (a person who travels to space).
Match astronaut kit to its job: sealed helmet → keeps in the air the astronaut breathes (the suit's backpack supplies the air), suit → protection for going outside.
Point to the picture that shows where astronauts live and work now (the ISS orbiting Earth).
Say whether people live on the Moon today (no — Apollo astronauts visited in the past; astronauts now live on the Station near Earth).
activities.title: Check and sort the key facts
